families.name: Deep breathing cue
families.meaning: Directs the listener to take a slow, deliberate breath, often specifying the route through the nose or mouth, to settle in.

families.name: Breath exhale route
families.meaning: Guides the listener to let breath out along a specific path, such as through the nose or mouth.

families.name: Settle and get comfortable
families.meaning: Prompts the listener to prepare the body and pause before the practice begins.

families.name: Eyes open and close
families.meaning: Instructs the listener to shift their eyes shut or open to mark the start or end of inward focus.

families.name: Readiness check
families.meaning: Tells the listener they have reached the point where the next stage can begin.

families.name: Permission and intention
families.meaning: Frames the instruction as the guide's wish or the listener's choice, softening the directive.

families.name: Imagined seeing and feeling
families.meaning: Asks the listener to picture or sense something, anchoring the visualization in perception.

families.name: Downward journey into body
families.meaning: Moves the listener's attention deeper, down through the body or inward toward a center.

families.name: Body awareness focus
families.meaning: Directs the listener's attention to noticing or inhabiting the body or its inner space.

families.name: Heart and center points
families.meaning: Names a specific anchor point in the body, such as the heart, crown, or center, for attention to rest on.

families.name: Return attention
families.meaning: Brings the listener's wandering attention back to the breath or the body.

families.name: Letting go and release
families.meaning: Invites the listener to release tension, thoughts, or control.

families.name: Calm and peace state
families.meaning: Describes or invites a feeling of peace, relaxation, safety or love as the desired state.

families.name: Reassurance of self
families.meaning: Affirms that a part of the listener's self is present, capable, or knows the way.

families.name: Repeat whenever
families.meaning: Tells the listener the practice can recur at any time or whenever needed.

families.name: Noticing change
families.meaning: Points out that the listener is shifting into a new condition, often as a natural result.

families.name: Continuing breath
families.meaning: Encourages the listener to keep breathing steadily through the session.
